Topic: What we learned about QUBO encoding
Scope: DuQuantum–Pasqal challenge research summary
Conclusion and limits: All quantum evidence here comes from simulators. No hardware or quantum advantage is demonstrated.

Topic: The defensible challenge conclusion
Scope: The strongest findings answer different questions
Conclusion and limits: A successful emulator run, a feasible assignment, and an exact encoded optimum are different outcomes.

Topic: How to read the experiments
Scope: Keep the testing layers separate
Conclusion and limits: Exact intended interactions are a diagnostic control. They need not be realizable by the hardware.

Topic: Encoding strategies we actually tried
Scope: Representation and atom counts precede the choice of optimizer
Conclusion and limits: Small / medium / large benchmark sizes: 4 / 10 / 15 customers. These are clustering encodings, not full routing encodings.

Topic: Added atoms and fitting methods
Scope: Two different redundancy constructions, plus the new ordering test
Conclusion and limits: Wire targets are partly known-answer informed. Earlier helper training uses exact low-energy states. New candidate generation avoids known optimum labels.

Topic: The compact prototype loses to a cheap control
Scope: 100 small problems, numerical final-state probabilities
Conclusion and limits: Separate earlier population: only 12 / 100 problems had active capacity constraints. Balanced control was added after execution.

Topic: Earlier representation pilots
Scope: Preserved negative results from the broader research branch
Conclusion and limits: Recursive feasible outputs had best clustering gaps of 110.28% and 177.45% on the two successful problems. Different populations are not pooled.

Topic: Capacity balance is not exact capacity enforcement
Scope: 100 fresh capacity-active problems, classical model checks
Conclusion and limits: Counts overlap: correct optima are a subset of feasible minima. Some balance weight succeeds on 96 / 100; no weight works on 4 / 100.

Topic: The strongest embedding isolation test
Scope: Number of layouts with at least one feasible minimum
Conclusion and limits: Small and 20-bit systems: exhaustive minima. Medium textbook: correctness and feasible-set bounds. Five endpoints never prepared.

Topic: Aggregate coupling error hides important failures
Scope: Relative pair-coefficient error, lower is better
Conclusion and limits: This is coefficient error, not quantum-state fidelity or solution error. Values can exceed one. All fitted geometries enter the summaries.

Topic: Strong penalties can hide the clustering signal
Scope: Large reduced BLaDE layouts illustrate the mismatch
Conclusion and limits: All five large instances show the pattern. The between-customer terms also contain balance contributions, so they are not objective-only.

Topic: Fields matter as well as pair interactions
Scope: Exhaustive static correction, 3 small and 5 medium problems
Conclusion and limits: 192 coefficient systems. This intervention is not a realizable layout or a quantum simulation. One medium target is itself suboptimal.

Topic: The main cloud benchmark is complete
Scope: 20 problems, both encodings, both placement methods
Conclusion and limits: 305 remote attempts include 4 failed attempts later replaced. Two reused accuracy references add no new samples. Charges unknown.

Topic: Small reduced encoding performs better
Scope: 10 problems, 3 placements per method, 60,000 shots per bar series entry
Conclusion and limits: Means first average placements within each problem. Large instance variation remains. Conservative penalties and one common pulse do not establish best possible performance.

Topic: Larger benchmark results remain poor
Scope: Primary fixed-policy quantum results
Conclusion and limits: Large textbook: BLaDE completed 14 / 15 with 0 / 28,000 feasible shots. Custom prepared 0 / 15. No medium or large main run found an optimum.

Topic: Small transfer test and classical controls
Scope: 6 small problems, mean optimal-clustering percentage
Conclusion and limits: Quantum: 4,000 shots per problem per variant. Random controls: 6,000 proposals. Individual controls are emulator-only. Transferred intended models later fail correctness checks.

Topic: Penalty tuning changes one small-case result
Scope: Single development problem, 10,000 cloud shots per condition
Conclusion and limits: Known-answer diagnostic. Physical follow-up changes penalties and geometry. The 59% decoded success is only 1.24% exact intended full-QUBO ground configurations.

Topic: Assignment success and full-QUBO success
Scope: Completed local state-vector study: 944 fresh trials, 680 case/arm evaluations
Conclusion and limits: Alternative known-answer formulations. Ranges are 3 search-seed means across 5 retrospective evaluation problems. Floor: 0.1%, not a certified upper bound.

Topic: Medium sampling falls after geometric translation
Scope: One 20-atom problem, original formulation, 20,000 cloud shots per arm
Conclusion and limits: Fine local references: 36.7942% versus 3.8912% feasible. Timestep halving changes feasibility by <0.0004 percentage points. Rare-category cloud discrepancies remain.

Topic: More placement effort does not repair solving
Scope: Completed subsets of the larger placement study
Conclusion and limits: The overall 5,400-fit placement campaign remains incomplete. Occupied-geometry validity does not mean solution validity. No cloud jobs in this static study.

Topic: Mathematical tuning gives mixed generalization
Scope: 80 trials: 40 adaptive and 40 random, with 24 fresh problems
Conclusion and limits: Both searches selected the same first random candidate. No adaptive-search advantage. Exact model enumeration only, no quantum dynamics. Measured compute: 2.454 seconds.

Topic: Weighted wires worsen medium energy fidelity
Scope: 3 medium reduced problems, effective-energy error
Conclusion and limits: Across all 9 problems, only 2 / 18 added-atom layouts improve logical-domain error. This recipe did not provide a generally successful fidelity intervention.

Topic: Weighted wires help small decoded sampling unevenly
Scope: Small textbook, geometric interactions, 4,000 shots per condition
Conclusion and limits: All 54 primary runs complete. All 3 medium reduced four-extra-atom arms show 0 / 4,000 feasible shots. Numerical refinements remain incomplete.

Topic: Free helpers improve one medium feasibility result
Scope: Matched refits, 2,000 cloud shots per arm and numerical setting
Conclusion and limits: 0 / 4,000 optimal shots per arm across both settings. Dominant feasible answers cost 68.48% above optimum. Training used exact low-energy target states.

Topic: Average-energy fitting is not enough
Scope: Longer free-helper fits on 5 medium problems
Conclusion and limits: All 30 longer fits hit the iteration limit. Of 40 helpers, 27 stay excited in every conditional minimum, consistent with bias adjustment. Error differs from pair-matrix error.

Topic: The expanded helper experiment is mixed
Scope: Snapshot report: 8:59 am ET, 37 / 46 jobs complete
Conclusion and limits: 2,000 shots per arm per problem. Small/medium means complete, large mean partial. No medium optimum observed. Stronger-setting checks remain incomplete.

Topic: The practical ordering experiment is now implemented
Scope: Three medium problems, 0 or 8 helpers, two objectives, three starts
Conclusion and limits: No cloud jobs in this stage. Candidate holdouts share the same 3 problems. Best classical candidates must be retained as the baseline.

Topic: What remains uncertain
Scope: The uncertainty changes what we can claim at the deadline
Conclusion and limits: Failed preparation is unmeasured. Zero observed success is not zero probability. A feasible clustering need not be a full encoded optimum or an optimal route.

Topic: Original notebook results vary sharply by problem
Scope: 25 calibratable four-atom problems from the original notebook study
Conclusion and limits: 1 / 26 original problems has no correct balance weight and was excluded by calibration. Manual performance exceeds 90% on 10 / 25. A strong single example is not representative.

Topic: Experiment inventory: mathematical and static tests
Scope: Distinct families, with overlapping instances explicitly retained
Conclusion and limits: Initial 66-candidate menu: later certificates resolve the 12 initially uncertain entries. A separate 90-case medium-textbook menu has 82 correct and 8 incorrect.

Topic: Experiment inventory: dynamics and scaling
Scope: Counts describe their own study, not an additive global total
Conclusion and limits: Local state-vector probabilities and shot estimates are different evidence. Reused references, layouts and problem instances are not independent repetitions.

Topic: Work still open at the evidence snapshot
Scope: Existing studies continue while this deck freezes the challenge evidence
Conclusion and limits: Snapshot collected at 9:01 am ET. Individual reports have their own earlier update times. No new scientific conditions were launched for this presentation.

Topic: Conclusions we can defend
Scope: A coherent result even when the proposed improvements fail
Conclusion and limits: The practical next test is already in progress: learn useful state ordering without supplying exact answers, and compare against the candidates found classically.
